search.title: Search
search.none: No results for “{q}”. Check the spelling or try a broader term, for example a civilization or region.
search.hint: Type a name such as Egypt, Rome or Maya. Search works across all site languages.

about.title: About this project
about.body1: History & Civilizations is a multilingual digital encyclopedia of human history, built to grow from a handful of pages to thousands.
about.body2: Every page follows one workflow: research, draft, source verification, human review, publish. Pages that have not completed review are marked as drafts.
about.body3: Images are only used when their license allows it, and each image carries its source, creator and license.

footer.disclaimer: Content marked as draft has not yet been fully verified against sources.

map.baseNote: The base map shows modern geography. Historical borders are not drawn yet.

tl.title: Interactive timeline

quiz.title: Quizzes
quiz.intro: Test what you know about a civilization. Answers and explanations appear at the end.
quiz.question: Question {n} of {m}

cmp.title: Compare civilizations
cmp.intro: Place two civilizations side by side. The comparison describes similarities and differences. It does not rank them.
cmp.note: Rows for military, science and culture are not included yet. Text is a short orientation and has not yet been verified page by page.

otd.title: On This Day
otd.intro: Historical events that happened on a given calendar date.
otd.none: No entry for this date in the current dataset.
otd.note: Dates of ancient events follow the Julian calendar, and precision at the level of the day varies. Only entries with a documented day are listed, and the list grows as verified entries are added.

mys.title: Historical mysteries
mys.intro: Open questions of the past. Each entry separates what is known from what is only proposed.
mys.note: Theories are presented as theories. Nothing here is offered as established fact unless the entry says so.

arch.intro: Sites and objects that carry the evidence for ancient history.

tech.intro: How ancient societies built, moved water and kept records.
